chunks: He (al-Mufid) said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad reported to me, he said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Isa ibn Mihran narrated to us, he said: Mukhawwal narrated to us, he said: al-Rabi' ibn al-Mundhir from his father narrated, who said: I heard al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) say:

"Indeed, Abu Bakr and Umar deliberately seized this affair (the Caliphate) while the whole of it belonged to us. They took it away from us and apportioned to us in it a share like the share of a grandmother (from an estate). By God, their own selves will be in deep anxiety on the day when people seek our intercession."

key_terms.الأمر: The affair, referring to the Caliphate and political authority
key_terms.سهم الجدة: Share of the grandmother, a minimal inheritance portion (one-sixth) in Islamic law, used metaphorically
key_terms.شفاعة: Intercession, the act of interceding on behalf of others on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Hasan say about Abu Bakr and Umar taking the Caliphate?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali (AS) declared that Abu Bakr and Umar deliberately took the Caliphate which rightfully belonged to the Ahl al-Bayt, giving them only a negligible share comparable to a grandmother's inheritance portion. He swore that the two would face grave distress on the Day of Judgment when people seek the intercession of the Prophet's household. This reflects the Shia position on the succession dispute after the Prophet's death, using legal inheritance language ("share of a grandmother") to emphasize how little was given to those who deserved everything.
